skill.name: agile-design-doc
skill.description: Creates concise agile design documents for software teams. It analyzes project context, identifies reusable components, and keeps designs focused on MVP delivery.
skill.summary: Create focused design documents that align new features with the existing project architecture.
skill.author: AriesYB

security_audit.summary: Static findings for command execution, reconnaissance, and obfuscation are false positives caused by Markdown fences, Mermaid diagrams, and multilingual prose. No malicious execution, prompt injection, or hidden code was found in the reviewed files. The only contextual risk is broad project file inspection, which is expected for this design-document workflow but should be scoped by users.

remediation.issue: The skill asks the assistant to inspect project files and directories.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short privacy note telling users to exclude secrets, credentials, and unrelated sensitive files from the workspace.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples use nested code fences that triggered static command and reconnaissance heuristics.
remediation.suggestion: Use indented examples or escaped fences in SKILL.md to reduce false positives during automated review.

content.value_statement: Teams often need fast design documents that avoid excessive scope. This skill turns project context into concise architecture, flow, and implementation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes project configuration files to identify languages, frameworks, and dependencies.
Maps reusable components from source directories, documentation, and user input.
Generates a concise design goal, feature list, interaction flow, and implementation plan.
Uses Mermaid diagrams to describe core component interactions.
Adds focused data model and API sections when the feature requires them.
Checks the draft for brevity, technical accuracy, and MVP scope.
limitations: It depends on available project files and user-provided feature context.
It does not validate code behavior or run architecture tests.
It may need manual review for unfamiliar frameworks or domain rules.
It favors MVP scope and may omit nonessential future enhancements.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Product Feature
use_cases.description: Create a short design document before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Align Backend API Changes
use_cases.description: Document service flow, data models, and endpoints for a backend change.

use_cases.title: Review Feature Scope
use_cases.description: Separate required MVP behavior from optional follow-up work.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Design Document
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an agile design document for this feature: [feature]. Use the current project structure and keep the scope MVP-focused.

prompt_templates.title: Use Existing Components
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request that needs reuse analysis.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this project for reusable components, then draft a design document for [feature]. Explain which components should be reused.

prompt_templates.title: Define API and Data Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a design document for [backend feature]. Include interaction flow, key methods, data model changes, and API definitions.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an Existing Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for review and scope control.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this design draft for MVP scope, technical accuracy, and duplication. Rewrite it into the agile design document format.

output_examples.input: Request a design document for user invitation support in an existing web application.
output: A clear design goal for invitation creation, delivery, and acceptance.
A short feature list that separates core behavior from later improvements.
A Mermaid sequence flow covering user, API, service, and storage interactions.
Implementation notes for key service methods and validation rules.

output_examples.input: Ask for a checkout redesign that must reuse existing order and payment modules.
output: A reuse-focused design that identifies existing order and payment components.
A concise interaction flow for cart, checkout API, payment service, and order persistence.
A brief risk section for payment failure, idempotency, and retry handling.

best_practices: Provide the feature goal, key user flow, and known constraints before running the skill.
Let the skill inspect relevant project files before asking for implementation details.
Review generated diagrams and API sections with the developers who own the components.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to produce long architecture proposals for small MVP changes.
Do not accept generated examples without checking them against real project code.
Do not include sensitive project files unless they are needed for the design task.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces concise design documents for agile software teams, including goals, feature scope, flows, and implementation notes.

faq.question: Does it inspect project files?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks the assistant to review configuration files, project structure, and documentation when available.

faq.question: Can it design APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can include API definitions when the requested feature changes service boundaries.

faq.question: Can it replace architecture review?
faq.answer: No. Developers should review the output for project constraints, security, and operational requirements.

faq.question: Is it only for Python projects?
faq.answer: No. It references Python, Node.js, Java, Go, and other project types through their configuration files.

faq.question: How should I get the best result?
faq.answer: Describe the feature goal, affected modules, existing constraints, and any components that must be reused.
